video.title: I built this app for my dad. Now it makes $18K/month

summary: Starter Story host Gus interviews Kurosh, a London-based product manager who built Boise (transcribed as 'Voice C'), a cross-platform dictation app using OpenAI's Whisper API, as a side project. It reportedly makes 16-20K USD per month including lifetime deals, with 11K MRR. He competes with well-funded tools like Whisper Flow by targeting seniors and people with disabilities, who see dictation as a painkiller rather than a vitamin. Growth comes mainly from SEO (about 200 blog posts, 30 landing pages, localisation), plus the Chrome Web Store, Reddit and a new YouTube series. Key takeaways: talk to users to discover your real customer, a crowded market can be won by serving a neglected niche, and take action in volume rather than strategising.

speakers.name: Kurosh
speakers.description: Founder of Boise (dictation app); Iranian-born, London-based former fintech product manager, learned to code from a book and now uses AI coding tools. Name is mis-heard in the transcript as Corush/Karash.

ideas.name: Boise dictation app for seniors and people with disabilities
ideas.one_liner: Cross-platform speech-to-text app built on OpenAI Whisper, aimed at older and disabled users who cannot type comfortably.
ideas.business_model: Subscription plus lifetime-deal one-off purchases, with a 20% disability discount
ideas.customer: Seniors, people with physical disabilities and others who cannot type without pain; also some professionals (60-70% of early users) wanting a productivity boost
ideas.problem: People who cannot type easily or comfortably on computers and phones need reliable dictation that works everywhere
ideas.offer: Dictation app using OpenAI Whisper API that works in any app on Windows, Mac, Linux, iOS, Android and as a Chrome extension

pricing.model: Monthly subscription plus lifetime plan, with discount for disabled users

price_points.label: disability discount, by emailing the founder

pricing.notes: Lifetime deals lift monthly cash revenue above MRR (11K MRR vs 16-20K monthly).

acquisition_channels.details: Chrome Web Store gave free traffic; asked five friends for reviews on day one and got 10-20 page views immediately; reached about the first 100 users.

quote.text: the Chrome web store where I posted a Chrome extension gives you like free traffic for basically zero work
quote.speaker: Kurosh

acquisition_channels.details: Posted a viral-angle post to subreddits five or six times until blocked, reaching about 200-300 users.

quote.text: I was also posting on Reddit like absolute crazy every day
quote.speaker: Kurosh

acquisition_channels.details: Main growth driver: about 200 blog posts, 30 landing pages, site localised into 4-5 languages; uses his own SEO tool Romeo SEO. Believes the first article in Google or AI search wins regardless of product quality.

quote.text: the true growth of voice C is from SEO
quote.speaker: Kurosh

acquisition_channels.details: Tutorial videos on speech to text and a series called AI for seniors; grew from about 1,000 to 12,000 subscribers in a month.

quote.text: We started like a YouTube series called AI for seniors and that one is taking off
quote.speaker: Kurosh

ideas.delivery: Software delivered via Chrome extension and native apps (Electron Windows app, Mac, Linux, iOS, Android) calling the Whisper API; built and maintained by the solo founder with AI coding tools (Cursor, Codex, Claude).
unit_economics_claims: 11K MRR but 16-20K per month total including lifetime deals
About 2,500 daily active users, 10,000 monthly active users, 1,400 active subscriptions
20% of users on the disability discount
Website on Framer costs about $200 per month; VPS about $40 per month
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; MVP built in about two weeks by the founder. Running costs include Framer ~$200/month, VPS ~$40/month, plus API costs.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; the Chrome extension got downloads without marketing soon after launch.

acquisition.how: SEO, blog and landing pages, app store listings and YouTube content are inbound channels that agents can largely produce and publish with occasional human review.

onboarding.how: Self-serve download, install and trial; the disability discount is via email and could be handled by an agent.

delivery.how: Pure software; the product runs unattended, though multi-platform app maintenance, OS updates and store releases need occasional human approval.

billing.how: Subscriptions and lifetime purchases via a payment processor are fully automated.

support.how: Seniors and disabled users likely need patient, high-touch help; agents can answer most queries with routine human checks.

uk_applicability.notes: Software sold globally; the founder runs it from London. Accessibility users are plentiful in the UK. Only needs UK VAT handling and GDPR for audio data.

risks: Well-funded competitors (Whisper Flow) could move into the senior market
Dependence on the OpenAI Whisper API and its pricing
Lifetime deals create future support and API costs without recurring revenue
Audio data privacy and GDPR obligations

tactics.name: Seed a Chrome extension launch with friend reviews
steps: Publish a simple extension to the Chrome Web Store
Ask about five friends to leave reviews on day one
Rely on store search for free traffic to reach the first ~100 users

quote.text: I asked like five friends to leave reviews, we instantly got like 10 or 20 page views
quote.speaker: Kurosh

tactics.name: Programmatic-scale SEO content
steps: Build many landing pages (about 30) for different use cases
Aim to be the first result people see in Google and AI search

quote.text: We have like 200 blog posts. We have like 30 different landing pages.
quote.speaker: Kurosh

tactics.name: Find the painkiller segment through user calls
steps: Talk to many users on calls
Segment them: 60-70% professionals wanting a 10% boost vs 20-30% seniors/disabled who need it
Notice who loves the MVP and does not demand improvements
Pivot positioning and content to that segment

quote.text: Those guys love the product. They didn't care about any improvements.
quote.speaker: Kurosh

tactics.name: Disability discount and lifetime deal pricing
steps: Offer a 20% discount to disabled users who email the founder
Sell a lifetime plan (~$260) alongside an $8.49 monthly plan to pull cash forward

tactics.name: Platform expansion with AI coding tools
steps: Start with a Chrome extension MVP in two weeks
Add Windows (Electron, ~3 months), then Mac (~1 month), Linux (~2 weeks), iOS and Android
Use Cursor, Codex and Claude to speed up builds

lessons.lesson: A crowded market can be entered by serving a segment that competitors ignore, here seniors and disabled users who are not talking about the well-funded tools.

quote.text: these older folks, they're not talking about Whisper Flow
quote.speaker: Kurosh

lessons.lesson: Sell painkillers, not vitamins: users who truly need the product tolerate an MVP and pay without demanding features.
User calls reveal the real customer; the ideal customer profile often picks you rather than the reverse.

quote.text: your ideal customer profile picks you
quote.speaker: Kurosh

lessons.lesson: In crowded markets the product the customer sees first often wins, so search visibility matters more than being best.

quote.text: it's not the best product that wins. It's the product that your customer sees first.
quote.speaker: Kurosh

lessons.lesson: Go for the easiest, lowest-barrier market early rather than the biggest.
Do high volume of content and experiments rather than strategising; quantity produces learning faster and quality follows.

quote.text: Just do the thing and do it five times more than you think you should.
quote.speaker: Kurosh

lessons.lesson: AI coding tools let a non-expert solo founder ship across many platforms quickly (Android app one-shotted, Linux in two weeks).
Lifetime deals boost cash revenue well above MRR, but MRR is the truer recurring base to compare.
Don't dismiss simple apps for non-tech audiences; many people outside the AI/Twitter bubble just want a problem solved.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand founder with specific metrics shown on a dashboard, but unverified on camera, no cost or margin detail, and Whisper tiny transcript has mis-heard names (Boise/Voice C, Kurosh). Revenue mixes lifetime sales with MRR.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes a free database of 50 AI app ideas (lead magnet). Founder promotes his own Romeo SEO tool.
